name: Sheffield Support Group
excerpt: About our group You can read the latest newsletter here. If you would like adding to the mailing list please call Val Heap on 0114 262 0468 or email [email protected]. You can also find us on Facebook, here. The ethos of the Sheffield Support Group is to support activities to enable people with Parkinson’s to build physical and mental wellness through participation in social events, learning and creative activities with like-minded people. The group is run for the charity by volunteers who are living with Parkinson’s themselves, or who have experience of Parkinson’s. It is supported by professional staff to: Offer information, friendship, and support to those with Parkinson’s, their carers, families and friends Organise or assist with events and social activities for members Raise funds for research to support people affected by Parkinson’s We believe that doing something positive for yourself is good for the soul. We arrange classes and activities that include: Posture and general fitness, Boxing, Pilates, Tango, Voice (singing), Saturday morning walks and monthly meetings, with a speaker, and an opportunity to meet others over a cup of tea A monthly drop in Parkinson’s Cafe held in Parson Cross Community Development Forum "A Positively Parkinson’s" group that holds monthly evening socials at the Waggon and Horses restaurant/pub on Abbeydale Road and is aimed at people aged 66 years and under A Supporters Group for those living with a person with Parkinson's We also signpost to privately run classes and other resources that may be of interest to people affected by Parkinson’s in the Sheffield area, eg: PD Warrior programme Personalised strength and fitness A machine-based circuits class We follow the values of Parkinson’s UK by putting People first and at the centre of decisions, Uniting all those who are affected by Parkinson’s in Sheffield, Pioneering with a can-do attitude and we are Driven to find a cure and offer support until one is found. Volunteers needed! We need to recruit volunteers to help us run the group. Do you have an hour or two per month to spare? If so we would be delighted to hear from you. For more information please email [email protected].

name: Birmingham South Support Group
excerpt: We aim to provide support to all those living with Parkinson’s which includes all spouses, partners and carers, as well as those who have been diagnosed. We organise a range of regular activities, which you can find more information about at the bottom of this page. Throughout the year, we also usually organise: A group trip to Birmingham Hippodrome panto in early January. A subsidised three course meal in early May. An annual Fundraising Quiz Night at Kings Heath Cricket Club in early August. A subsidised Christmas Meal at Kings Heath Cricket Club in early December. A weekend away at Warners Studley Castle Hotel in June. Membership of the group is FREE to join, and we ask you to make a contribution, usually £3, to most activities on the door. Our fundraising events include our annual quiz night and monthly Crafty Natters, and we aim to hold a variety of events to appeal to the wider public outside the group. The group is run by a committee of volunteers, who meet once a month. View our January to June calendar of events here and July to December calendar here. See our Facebook page here.

name: Blackfen Support Group
excerpt: Come rain or shine we meet for a coffee and chat at a lovely community cafe in Blackfen every month. Our members in their own words describe the group as very welcoming - offering people with Parkinson’s, carers and family mutual support, friendship and often fun. This sociable get together allows everyone to share experiences, good and bad, and to not feel so isolated in dealing with Parkinson’s. Free to attend, just buy your own refreshments. Family and friends welcome. You’ll find us in the Blackfen Community Library, please get in touch with Debbie if you'd like to find out more or come along and visit the group. Hope to see you there! You can find more information about our monthly cafe meeting here and watch our YouTube video here.

name: Guildford and South Surrey Branch
excerpt: Our branch has over 350 members. They are mainly people who have Parkinson's, but our membership also includes carers, families, and friends. We keep in touch by post, email, and our website: www.guildfordparkinsons.org.uk. Members can take part in numerous activities, from exercise, dance, singing and speech maintenance classes, to outings, fundraising events, meetings and social gatherings. To become a member, please complete the online form on the branch membership page of our website. Every third Wednesday of each month we meet at the Squirrel Inn, Godalming, from 7.00 pm. Most members order something to eat as there is a varied menu from which to order a meal or a dessert and coffee. Formerly called the Working Age Group (WAG) this group is now known as the Friendship Group. Anyone is welcome to attend this informal get-together. For more details visit https://www.guildfordparkinsons.org.uk/social-activities/wednesday-evening-social-meetings/ Our monthly branch social meetings are an informal get-together. Afternoon social meetings, often with a guest speaker, are held on the last Tuesday of each month and all branch members, their partners, carers or family members are welcome to attend. For more details visit https://www.guildfordparkinsons.org.uk/social-activities/tuesday-afternoon-social-meetings/ A social meeting for the newly diagnosed aims to provide support for people with Parkinson’s at a sensitive time in their lives. These Recently Diagnosed gatherings are held in-person. For more details visit https://www.guildfordparkinsons.org.uk/social-activities/recently-diagnosed-social-meetings/ Details of groups, meetings, gatherings and events also appear in “The Park", our free newsletter which is issued three times a year. name: Horsham and District Branch
excerpt: For more information about our group, contact us or visit our website: https://horsham.parkinsonsuk.group/ Our local group offers friendship and support to people with Parkinson’s, their families, and carers. For information and advice on Parkinson’s, or emotional support, call the Parkinson’s UK helpline on 0808 800 0303. Our branch organizes various popular activities four days a week, almost every week of the year. We believe that keeping moving is crucial in Parkinson’s to slow its progression and enhance overall quality of life. It’s essential to find activities that suit your interests, are enjoyable, and supervised by specialists in the specific activity to maximize benefits and minimize the risk of injury. We’ve categorized our activities into three intensity levels: high, medium, and low. For more details, visit our website. Each activity is associated with a contact point. We provide information and timings for these activities, and we also have an online calendar to keep you updated on what’s happening. We recognise the importance of socialisation and problem-solving for individuals with Parkinson’s. We offer two types of meetings: a branch meeting where we invite speakers to discuss various topics, and a working-age group social meeting held in a pub. This latter meeting provides a more informal setting for confidential conversations with other Parkinson’s-affected individuals. For more information, visit our website. Our branch is supported by a team of friendly volunteers, but we always welcome others who would like to contribute. In addition to our local activities, we fundraise to support local activities, research, Parkinson’s nurses, and other services. If you’re interested in helping, please get in touch.

name: Online Working Age / Newly Diagnosed Carers Support Group
excerpt: The group is open to all carers and family members aged over 18 and under 67 supporting someone newly diagnosed with Parkinson’s. You do not have to be a registered carer. It's free to join. The informal online sessions are facilitated by volunteers with caring experience and a chance to talk with people in similar situations, share experiences, and support each other. We aim for the group to provide mutual support to those living with or caring for a person diagnosed with Parkinson’s within (approximately) the last 3 years. If you do not meet the newly diagnosed or age criteria, we host another online carers support group, which you are welcome to join. For carers under the age of 18, we suggest finding a group specifically aimed for young carers would best meet your needs. This online group is for peer-to-peer support and is not monitored by professional advisers. If participants want additional or one-to-one support, they may be signposted by volunteers to other groups, services, or other Parkinson’s UK support opportunities. Places are limited to 15 to help ensure people feel supported and listened to. The group is closed and we plan to only take new participants if space becomes available after the first six sessions. This is to allow the group to build trusting relationships with the same people. If the group becomes oversubscribed, a waiting list will be created for people wanting to join the next six sessions. Join our session on the 3rd Wednesday of the month, from 7pm to 8.30pm. To book a place, please contact Satpal using the contact details below. When booking, please provide your name, email address, telephone number, and address.
